item.title: Soul Candi Institute launches national recruitment drive in SA
item.description: The Soul Candi Institute of Music & Record Label has launched a national student recruitment campaign to coincide with the start of its new academic cycle. The campaign began earlier this month and will run until the second week of February 2026. It targets prospective musicians, producers, DJs, vocalists, songwriters and music entrepreneurs across the country. Soul Candi, based in Rosebank, has produced graduates who have gone on to work across various areas of the music and creative industries

item.title: Spotify: Meet the artists rewriting Africa’s sonic future
item.description: While 2024 marked the year African music cemented its global export status, 2025 has been a year of introspection and reinvention. item.title: YouTube CEO outlines 2026 priorities, focus on AI content, creator innovation
item.description: YouTube CEO Neal Mohan has outlined the company’s priorities for 2026, emphasising efforts to manage low-quality AI-generated content and support creators experimenting with new formats. The announcement comes amid ongoing tensions with Billboard, after YouTube Music declined to share data for chart rankings. item.title: South African radio presenter Njinji dies
item.description: The South African entertainment industry is mourning the death of radio presenter and former Ukhozi FM host, Njinji, who passed away on 24 January. News of his death sparked an outpouring of tributes on social media, with fellow broadcasters, musicians and media personalities from Durban remembering him as a passionate and influential figure in the city’s radio culture. Former Vuma FM presenter Jacinta Ngobese Zuma posted on social media: “Eish Mfethu ulale ngoxolo.” (Oh brother, rest in peace).

item.title: GEMA to sell Zebralution to DistroKid investor Insight Holdings
item.description: German collecting society GEMA has agreed to sell digital distribution company Zebralution to the US-based investment firm Insight Holdings Group, a key investor in DistroKid. The transaction is subject to regulatory approval. GEMA confirmed that it will sell 100 per cent of Zebralution to Insight Holdings, which invests through its growth equity arm, Insight Partners.
